minutes.headline: Parks Commission picked Ray Dunit Landscape Architecture (RDLA) as top choice for Marshall Park design after three interviews.
minutes.summary: The commission interviewed three landscape design firms (Fuss & O'Neill, Nezra/NRA-style engineering team, and RDLA with Vision Sports Design and Meridian), reviewed reference checks and fee proposals, and chose RDLA by motion. It also approved the revolving fund limit submitted by the town manager's office and reviewed draft special town meeting warrant articles.

votes.motion: Move forward with RDLA as the top choice firm for Marshall Park design
Approve the Parks Commission revolving fund as submitted to the chair by the town manager's office

budget_items.what_was_said: The RFP capped phase one at a not-to-exceed amount; one firm's fee excluded bidding support and construction administration. Totals for phase one, phase two and overall were compared across firms.

The town manager's office proposed a spending limit from the revolving account, with a balance at end of FY24 and expected revenue yet to come. The limit can be raised by another vote if recreation director hours increase.

budget_items.topic: Recreation director hours funded from revolving fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Warrant article would raise the hours, funded from the revolving fund, with discussion of a maximum above the initial figure.
Draft article to borrow within the debt limit under chapter 44 section 10, without a debt exclusion or ballot question.
The town received a park grant, awaits a decision on another grant tied to Army Corps permitting, and did not receive the trails grant; an ADA application is pending.

budget_items.topic: Additional funding at November special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: Firms were asked how they would produce an updated cost number in time for November town meeting.

decisions.decision: Reference-check results would not change scoring; all firms scored evenly and rankings stay as established.
Town's interim manager's office/Julie to start the contract with RDLA; OPM has a meeting set for Monday and will press urgency.
Unselected firms will not be notified until the contract with the chosen firm is signed.
Chair will review the draft special town meeting articles with town counsel on Monday; warrant article for recreation hours to be phrased as up to a maximum.
Next regular meeting set for the third Wednesday in September, the 18th, at 7 o'clock.

Interview 3: RDLA with Vision Sports Design and Meridian
Deliberation on firms, references and fee proposals
Vote selecting RDLA and next steps on contract

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to move forward with Ray Dunit Landscape Architecture (RDLA) as its top-choice firm for the Marshall Park design.
The commission approved the Parks Commission revolving fund limit as submitted to the chair by the town manager's office.
The town manager's office is to start the contract with RDLA, and unselected firms will not be told until that contract is signed.
The commission reviewed draft special town meeting articles, including borrowing for Marshall Park within the debt limit, without a debt exclusion or ballot question; no vote was taken.
The next regular meeting was set for the third Wednesday in September, the 18th, at 7 o'clock.

why_it_matters: The design firm chosen here shapes the cost estimate for Marshall Park, and the draft borrowing article would put that cost before residents at a special town meeting without a ballot vote on a debt exclusion.
The revolving fund limit sets how much the commission may spend from fees it collects, including recreation director hours, and the limit can be raised by another vote.
watch_next: The special town meeting warrant articles on Marshall Park borrowing and recreation director hours, which the chair was to review with town counsel on Monday.
Signing of the RDLA contract, and whether an updated cost number is ready for the November special town meeting.

Ours has the fee figures, hours and several procedural decisions the official minutes omit, and the official minutes add the presenters, the absent member and the $2 million concern. The one substantive difference to check is scoring: ours says all firms scored evenly, while the official minutes say scoring was deferred until after the interviews.
